chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talhah ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The neighbour is like the self, without causing harm nor being a sinner.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ethical standard for treating neighbours according to hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elevates the neighbour to the status of the self, establishing a legal and spiritual imperative to avoid both material harm (darar) and moral transgression (ithm). This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on neighbourly rights (haqq al-jar) as a fundamental component of social justice and individual piety. The teaching reflects the broader Islamic principle that ethical conduct towards neighbours is inseparable from one's overall standing before God.
